input.null_pointer_behavior: Null input returns -1 at declared lengths 0 and 105.

output.meaning: Total number of (pattern, start-position) exact matches, including overlapping matches.

algorithm_profile.preprocessing: Build a trie of reversed patterns; compute shift1 from all proper suffix-related trie nodes, shift2 by terminal suffix candidates propagated from the parent, and the bad-character depth table.
algorithm_profile.search: Start at the shortest-pattern window end, walk right-to-left through the reversed trie, count every terminal node reached, then advance by min(shift2[v], max(shift1[v], char[c]-depth(v)-1)).
algorithm_profile.overlap: Every pattern terminal reached during a trie walk is counted; positive safe shifts preserve overlapping occurrences.
algorithm_profile.complexity: For T trie nodes, P patterns and text length N, direct bounded table construction is O(T^2*L) by suffix comparison; matching is O(N*L) worst case for L<=8, with skipping in typical inputs.
algorithm_profile.distinctness: Unlike Aho-Corasick, this scans alignments right-to-left on a reverse trie and advances using Commentz-Walter good-suffix and bad-character tables; it does not visit every text symbol in one forward automaton pass.

oracle_method: Primary: deterministic Commentz-Walter B reverse-trie search with the two safe-shift tables and bad-character table. Independent: compare every pattern against every possible text start directly.

source.primary_citation: Beate Commentz-Walter, A string matching algorithm fast on the average, Proceedings of the 6th International Colloquium on Automata, Languages and Programming, LNCS 71, 118-132, 1979.
source.reuse: The algorithm description and bibliographic facts were used; no implementation code or upstream benchmark frames were copied.
